title: Legacy endpoint deprecation: client SLA & migration timeline
creator: Asha Khandelwal
description: This ticket defines the commercial and technical migration contract for deprecating the legacy /v0/generate and /v0/stream endpoints. The goal is to provide a clear SLA-backed migration window for customers, set acceptance criteria for client compatibility tools, and document a timeline and rollback guarantees. This PRD covers requirements for notices, SDK compatibility guarantees, throttled dual-run window, billing protections, and legal communications to enterprise customers.
scope: Define 6-month migration timeline and 9-month hard-deprecation date
SLA guarantee: maintain 99.9% availability for legacy traffic routed via compatibility gateway during transition
Billing protection: customers will receive credits for errors introduced by migration changes within first 60 days
SDK compatibility: ship client adapter libraries for JavaScript, Python, Java with opt-in middleware
Provide a one-click console toggle for customers to enter ‘compat mode’ that routes to fallback variants
out_of_scope: On-prem appliance changes outside Redwood Private contract
Model-level changes beyond alias mapping (e.g., fine-tuning model semantics)
acceptance_criteria: Public deprecation notice published with dates and migration resources
Compatibility gateway implemented and load-tested at 2x expected legacy traffic
Client adapter libraries published with automated backwards-compat tests and 30-day deprecation warnings in logs
Billing protection workflow documented and tested (credits issued within 3 business days of verified regression)
Enterprise notification pack and escalation path approved by legal and support
migration_steps: T-minus 180d: Publish deprecation announcement and migration guide; open support inbox; start enterprise outreach
T-minus 150d: Release client adapter betas and migration-checker CLI; invite top 50 customers to private beta
T-minus 120d: Launch compatibility gateway (read-path translation + fallback routing) behind toggle
T-minus 90d: Begin dual-run telemetry collection and automated regression detection against migration test prompts
T-minus 60d: Enable console ‘compat mode’ for opt-in; start enforcing throttled redirects for small percentage of legacy traffic
T-minus 30d: Full opt-in window closed; send final reminder and provide migration support sprints
Deprecation date (T+0): Disable legacy write endpoints for new tokens; maintain read-only compatibility gateway for 90 days as emergency fallback
Post-deprecation +30d: Issue initial usage credits where regressions were verified
Post-deprecation +90d: Sunset compatibility gateway and close migration exceptions
rollback_criteria: If error rate for customer critical routes > 1% sustained for 60 minutes after migration step
If latency regressions cause 50% increase in P99 compared to baseline for two consecutive hours
If automated quality checks flag semantic regressions > 0.5% for prioritized prompt sets
If enterprise legal escalations require preservation of legacy behavior per contract
communication_plan: Week 0: Blog post + docs page with migration checklist and guide
Week 1-4: Targeted emails to top 500 active users with account-specific migration notes
Ongoing: Office hours weekly (AMER/EU/APAC rotation) and migration office hours recording library
Pre-deprecation (30/14/7 days): Reminder emails + console banners + in-SDK deprecation warnings
Incident channel: #prod-migrations and prioritized support queue for enterprise customers
rollout_timeline: 2026-05-01: Start throttled redirects and dual-run telemetry (T-60)
2026-06-30: Hard deprecation date for write endpoints (T+0)
metrics: Migration adoption rate (percentage of active customers migrated by date)
Error rate delta (post-migration vs baseline) per customer
P99 latency delta for priority routes
Number and severity of enterprise escalations
risks: Large customers with embedded on-prem clients cannot upgrade within window
Compatibility gateway introduces unanticipated latency for high-throughput customers
Billing protection process could be abused leading to revenue leakage
Insufficient SDK adoption delays migration progress
mitigations: Offer extended migration SLAs for enterprise customers on a case-by-case basis
Performance budget: compatibility gateway must add <10ms median latency for <95% of requests
Fraud detection rules around credit issuance and manual review for large claims
Developer enablement: migration playbooks, automated fixes in adapter libraries, migration sprints with solutions engineering
open_questions: What is the legal minimum notice period for customers in EEA?
Do we require signed migration amendments for Enterprise customers with dedicated capacity?
Which internal priority prompt sets must be used for automated semantic regression checks?
Do we expose a billing-protection API for partners to programmatically request credits?
